text:
Jordan (support): Customer (AcmeApp) reporting intermittent 502s from hosted API /v1/generate since ~2026-03-16T02:14Z after our cert rotation window. They see 'tls: handshake timeout' and sometimes DNS failures. Attached their logs.

Maya (oncall): Thanks. Can you paste a short sample curl they used?

Jordan (support): They ran:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  --data '{"prompt":"hello"}' --max-time 10
```
Response: early SSL/TLS handshake failure then gateway 502.

Eli (eng-infra): @Maya @Jordan on it. Suspect resolver rotation hitting a blackholed server in the pool. Any trace ids or customer path ids?

Jordan (support): Trace id: trace=acme-987654321. Edge logs show upstream DNS connect timeouts to 10.2.4.11:53, repeated SERVFAIL then fallback to 10.2.4.12 which sometimes succeeds.

Maya (oncall): Ask customer to run these probes and paste outputs — helps repro from their network:
```
dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example A
dig +short @10.2.4.11 api.redwood.example A
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -servername api.redwood.example -tlsextdebug -state
```

Eli (eng-infra): Also capture a short tcpdump for ports 53 and 443 (from their client or our region bastion):
```
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 '(port 53 or port 443)' -w /tmp/acme.pcap -c 500
```

Acme Support (customer): Running now. Results: `dig @8.8.8.8` -> 35.214.10.23. `dig @10.2.4.11` -> timeout. `openssl s_client` shows "no peer certificate" for some attempts, and `ssl handshake` failure on others. Attached pcap (truncated).

Maya (oncall): :eyes: That looks like a resolver blackhole. @Eli can infra rotation logs show anything around 02:10-02:18 UTC?

tam (eng-infra): Checking rotation logs... I see a partial DNS server delist during the rotation window for region-us-west2 (02:10-02:18 UTC). Health check marked 10.2.4.11 unreachable and it was re-added without the updated firewall rule. That caused UDP/53 to be dropped for that IP — clients got SERVFAIL or timeouts and sometimes fell back to TCP which increased DNS latency and triggered TLS handshake timeouts upstream.

Eli (eng-infra): Ok. Short-term mitigation: enable resolver fallback to public resolvers for hosted API routes in region-us-west2 and enable TCP fallback/retries for DNS client. I'll push emergency config.

tam (eng-infra): Workaround applied at 02:47 UTC for region-us-west2 (enabled public-resolver fallback). Monitoring.

Jordan (support): Customer confirms a significant drop in 502s after 02:50. They saw one residual spike at ~02:49 but stable after 02:50. :thumbsup: 

Maya (oncall): Quick RCA summary: DNS node removed during rotation ended up behind a firewall change; UDP DNS dropped -> repeated SERVFAILs and higher DNS latency -> TLS handshake timeouts at the gateway manifested as 502s to customers. Action items: 
- eng-infra (tam): add pre-rotation firewall sanity check + blocklist validation (ticket INF-4823, ETA 48h)
- eng-runtime (Eli): make resolver fallback public after N SERVFAILs and enable TCP fallback tests (ticket RTE-1298, ETA 72h)
- support (Jordan): send customer follow-up and postmortem once infra + runtime tickets are triaged

tam (eng-infra): Confirmed INF-4823 created.

Eli (eng-infra): Confirmed RTE-1298 created.

Jordan (support): Will send customer update now and close escalation if stable for 24h. Thanks everyone. (reaction :thumbsup: by Maya)
